Dongfeng Motor Corp Sees Steady Growth in Latest Results

Dongfeng Motor Corp reported stable financial and operational results for its most recent quarter, reflecting consistent demand in China's automotive sector and continued progress on the company’s electrification initiatives. The state-owned automaker posted a 4.5% year-on-year rise in revenue, reaching RMB 34.8 billion, while net profit grew by 3.2% to RMB 1.86 billion.

Company executives attributed the positive performance to robust sales of new energy vehicles (NEVs) and firm demand in the commercial vehicle segment. “Our focus on innovation and efficiency has allowed Dongfeng Motor Corp to deliver solid results in a competitive environment,” said Vice President Zhang Wei during an earnings call. “We are seeing encouraging order volumes for our latest electric models, especially in tier-two and tier-three cities.”

Industry analysts echoed this sentiment, noting Dongfeng’s balanced approach to traditional and new energy products. “Dongfeng’s diversified product mix is helping it weather market fluctuations, while its investments in NEV technology are beginning to bear fruit,” commented Li Chun, auto sector analyst at the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers.

According to Dongfeng, the company delivered 162,000 vehicles in the quarter, up 5.1% from a year ago. NEV sales accounted for 16% of total deliveries, marking a record high for the group. The automaker also reaffirmed its full-year guidance and stated it continues to strengthen cooperation with domestic supply partners such as Yujin Components.

“Looking ahead, we remain confident in our ability to meet the changing preferences of Chinese consumers and to contribute to the industry’s transition to cleaner mobility,” Zhang added.
